instagram.enables: Publishing Reels to your own account through the official Instagram Platform API. As the app owner you stay in Meta's Standard Access: no App Review and no Business Verification.

threads.enables: Publishing posts to your own Threads account through the official Threads API. Same Meta app as Instagram; owner use is Standard Access: no App Review, no Business Verification.

messenger.enables: Messenger auto-reply and DM features on your Page. Messenger keeps its own connect flow; this status line shows the same Meta app.

facebook.enables: Page-scoped publishing through the Graph API. Facebook keeps its own ``xpst auth facebook`` flow; this status line shows its stored app.

tiktok.enables: Direct-posting to your own TikTok account through the official Content Posting API. Unaudited apps post SELF_ONLY (private) until TikTok audits the app — xPST never claims public reach it does not have.

stdout_json.note: One Meta app covers Instagram, Threads and Messenger: enter it once and both platforms pick it up. Secrets live only in the encrypted store under the xPST config dir and are never echoed back.

video_envelope.source: YouTube Data API v3 videos.insert (resumable upload); YouTube upload limits: 12 hours / 256 GB; Shorts: ≤ 60 s, square or taller than wide
video_envelope.note: Both modes use the same resumable videos.insert call; the mode decides the title tag, the returned URL, and which ceiling is enforced.

content.note: two real modes: short-form (Shorts, ≤ 60 s, square-or-vertical, '#Shorts' tag, /shorts/ URL) and long-form (resumable videos.insert, watch URL, up to 12 h / 256 GB). The mode is explicit (--shorts/--long) or derived from the media probe; a video that fits neither is refused with both ceilings in the message.
no carousel path: a carousel request is refused by name, and nothing is stitched into a video

video_envelope.source: X media upload limits: 140 s of video for standard accounts, 512 MB, 1:2.39-2.39:1; Premium accounts allow longer videos (raise it with x.max_video_duration_seconds)
video_envelope.note: No long-form path until the account's real cap is raised; over 140 s is refused, never truncated.

content.note: single image post (upload_image): JPG/PNG/WEBP, ≤ 5 MB, aspect 1:3–3:1
published as a tweet thread, one media item per tweet (upload_carousel), in the given order; image items are checked against X's image contract before upload
one text post (280 characters max); no media, published via post_text
not declared: a text-only thread has no sender. Multi-media posting works as a tweet thread and is reported as carousel.

video_envelope.source: Meta Reels API: Reels up to 15 minutes, 4 GB

content.note: feed photo (upload_image): JPEG only, ≤ 8 MB, aspect within 4:5–1.91:1; the Graph API path needs a public image URL and refuses a local file explicitly
native album upload (2-10 items, order preserved); image items are checked against Instagram's image contract before the album call; over 10 items or under 2 is refused, never truncated

video_envelope.source: TikTok Content Posting API: video up to 10 minutes, 1 GB

content.note: no carousel path: a carousel request is refused by name, and nothing is stitched into a video

tiktok.note: video is implemented on two routes: xPST's own Content Posting API route is blocked by TikTok app review, and the rented aggregator route (accounts.tiktok.provider: zernio) publishes publicly through the vendor's audited app; there is no carousel path on either route

threads.media_transport_requirement: Threads has no upload endpoint: its API fetches your media from a public server, and xPST is a local tool with no server to host a file for it. A local file cannot be published to Threads, and xPST cannot deliver a media URL either yet — post this content from the Threads app instead.

video_envelope.source: Threads API: video up to 5 minutes (the container fetches it from a public URL)

content.note: published only from media that is already hosted at a public URL: the Threads API retrieves the URL itself and has no binary upload, so a local file is refused before any network call (see media_transport). xPST cannot deliver a media URL to any uploader yet either, so no media publishing path reaches Threads today
no carousel path: a carousel request is refused by name, and nothing is stitched into a video
one text post (500 characters max) via the TEXT container, no media needed

threads.note: Threads is a URL-fetch destination for media: it publishes what it can download from a public URL, never a local file — and xPST cannot hand it a URL yet, so media publishing is refused today. Text posts need no URL and are published verbatim through a media_type TEXT container.

video_envelope.source: Graph API /{page-id}/videos: up to 4 hours, 10 GB

facebook.note: Page-scoped: publishes as a Facebook Page, never as a personal profile (there is no API for that). Feed video today; Reels / photo / text are the follow-up that extends this row.

video_envelope.source: Rumble video upload API is partner-gated; limits are reported by the service per plan
video_envelope.note: Integration-uncertain: no self-serve developer console, so the manual handoff is the reliable path.

content.note: long-form only (Rumble is a video platform, not a Shorts surface). Two paths: the partner upload API when an API key is configured, and a MANUAL HANDOFF otherwise — the rendition and a caption file are written to a directory you choose, and the adapter reports the handoff instead of pretending it uploaded.

rumble.note: integration-uncertain: Rumble's upload API is partner-gated with no self-serve developer console comparable to Meta/Google. xPST declares the capability and both paths, but does not advertise Rumble as ready until one live upload succeeds.

content.note: no video path: Bluesky serves video from a separate service (video.bsky.app) with an asynchronous upload job, and xPST will not claim it until a live upload proves it — a video request is refused by name
single image post (upload_image): JPG/PNG/WEBP/GIF, ≤ 2,000,000 bytes, uploaded as a PDS blob and embedded in the post record
native multi-image post (upload_carousel): 2-4 images in one app.bsky.embed.images embed, order preserved; over 4 is refused with the number, never cut down
one post (300 characters max) via post_text; links are faceted so they are clickable

bluesky.note: Open posting API (AT Protocol): an app password or OAuth session is the whole gate — no review, no fee, no developer console. Text, image and multi-image posts only.

content.note: send_text delivers a direct message, not a public post

messenger.note: messaging destination: DMs only, never a publishing target. Its upload() is a text-DM shim (the abstract upload contract reused to deliver a message), not a video publish.

threads.media_transport_requirement: Threads has no upload endpoint: its API fetches your media from a public server, and xPST is a local tool with no server to host a file for it. A local file cannot be published to Threads, and xPST cannot deliver a media URL either yet — post this content from the Threads app instead.

Kick publishes no chat read endpoint: /public/v1/chat is send and delete only, and the documented alternative is the chat.message.sent webhook event, which needs a registered app and a public callback. Community libraries still point at a public Pusher app key that Kick has retired (Pusher answers 4001 on every cluster); kick.com's own page now mints an anonymous guest token at web.kick.com/api/v1/realtime/auth/connection and connects to its own Centrifugo service. Connection, subscription and heartbeat are proven from this repository; no chat publication has been observed yet, so the row stays unverified.

stdout_json.name: xpst_run
stdout_json.description: Check for new videos and cross-post them to configured platforms. A batch where nothing was published is never reported as success: `batch_status` says `published` / `partial` / `failed` / `nothing_to_do`, `exit_code` is the status the CLI would exit with, and `failed_destinations` names every destination that failed.

stdout_json.name: xpst_post
stdout_json.description: Post to platforms: one local video/image file, a carousel (carousel_paths), or a text post. `content_type` states what the post is in the canonical vocabulary (video/image/carousel/text/thread); a type a chosen destination cannot publish is refused with an explicit blocker BEFORE anything is uploaded, and the refusal is never reported as a success. `overrides` writes a different caption per destination (e.g. {"x": {"text": "short copy"}}); destinations without one use `caption`. Call `xpst_capabilities` to see what each destination can actually publish.

stdout_json.name: xpst_analytics
stdout_json.description: Per-post and per-platform engagement metrics (views, likes, comments, shares) with persisted snapshot history. live=false reads the local snapshot store only (fast, offline); live=true refreshes from the platform APIs first. Every platform reports collection_status (ok/partial/failed/unavailable/unknown) with its error: a failed collection is labelled, never returned as a silent zero.

stdout_json.name: xpst_cross_post_analytics
stdout_json.description: Cross-post correlation analytics (B1): one video posted to multiple platforms shown as a single entry with aggregated totals (views, likes, comments, shares) and per-platform breakdown, plus engagement rate and tier (high/medium/low). Reads the local snapshot store only — fast and offline.

stdout_json.name: xpst_followers
stdout_json.description: Follower counts per platform with growth history. Returns total followers across all platforms, per-platform counts, and recent growth trends from stored snapshots.

stdout_json.name: xpst_best_time
stdout_json.description: Best time to post per platform, based on engagement history. Analyzes when your posts get the highest engagement and recommends the optimal day-of-week and hour for each platform.

stdout_json.name: xpst_security_audit
stdout_json.description: Run an automated security check on the xPST installation. Verifies credential file permissions, encrypted storage, dashboard localhost binding, MCP readonly mode, FFmpeg availability, and provider mode configuration.

stdout_json.name: xpst_suggest_caption
stdout_json.description: Generate AI caption suggestions for a video file. Uses the video's transcript to generate 3 caption variants with platform-specific character limits and hashtag suggestions. Falls back to deterministic extraction when no LLM is configured.

stdout_json.name: xpst_generate_ideas
stdout_json.description: Generate post ideas for a content topic (AI content studio). Uses the KB LLM when configured (XPST_KB_LLM_ENABLED), otherwise falls back to deterministic template generation — no LLM required. Returns up to `count` ideas, each with an 'idea' headline and optional 'hook'.

stdout_json.name: xpst_transcript
stdout_json.description: Get the transcript for a video by its content_hash or video_id. Returns the full transcript text and segment timestamps. Transcripts are cached by content_hash so cross-posted videos share the same transcript (D2).

stdout_json.name: xpst_search
stdout_json.description: Search the knowledge base for nuggets, clips, and topics. Returns matching knowledge nuggets with their source video info and analytics correlation (total views across platforms).

stdout_json.name: xpst_activity
stdout_json.description: List recorded platform failures with targeted retry or review actions (read-only)

stdout_json.name: xpst_schedule_list
stdout_json.description: List scheduled posts (pending, completed, failed) with times and targets

stdout_json.name: xpst_schedule_add
stdout_json.description: Schedule a post for later: local video file + caption + ISO-8601 time, optional platform list, repeat rule (daily/weekly/monthly), and per-destination caption overrides (honoured when it fires). Omit video_path for a text-only post: caption IS the post, stored as content_type=text and fired through the text route.

stdout_json.name: xpst_schedule_cancel
stdout_json.description: Cancel a scheduled post by entry id — the MCP equivalent of `xpst schedule remove`. Removes the entry from the LOCAL schedule store (~/.xpst/schedule.json) only; it never un-posts content that has already been published. Get entry ids from xpst_schedule_list. dry_run=true returns the same verdict without modifying the store. An unknown id is an error (POST_NOT_FOUND), never a silent success.

stdout_json.name: xpst_schedule_pause
stdout_json.description: Pause the schedule queue — the MCP equivalent of `xpst schedule pause`. No scheduled entry fires (from cron, the daemon or an explicit run) until xpst_schedule_resume. Safe to call: it stops posts, never starts them.

stdout_json.name: xpst_schedule_resume
stdout_json.description: Release a paused schedule queue — the MCP equivalent of `xpst schedule resume`. Due entries become eligible to fire again; this re-enables publishing, so it is a consent-gated mutation.

stdout_json.name: xpst_failures_retry
stdout_json.description: Retry ONE recorded upload failure, identified by video_id + platform — the MCP equivalent of `xpst failures retry <video_id> --platform <name>`. Re-posts that video's local source file to that single destination (a REAL platform upload; scope=platform_upload). Returns ok=false with VIDEO_NOT_FOUND, NO_RECORDED_FAILURE, NO_LOCAL_FILE or RETRY_FAILED instead of pretending a retry happened; posted=true only when the destination accepted the post. Use xpst_activity to list failures and their retryable flag, and dry_run=true to plan without uploading.

stdout_json.name: xpst_health
stdout_json.description: Test connectivity to all platforms and sources (no uploads)

stdout_json.name: xpst_status
stdout_json.description: Show cross-posting statistics and health status

stdout_json.name: xpst_rate_limit_status
stdout_json.description: Read-only view of active rate-limit cooldowns: per platform the remaining seconds, strike count, resume time and the platform's recorded reason. A cooldown defers posts, it does not fail them. Pure local read — no uploads, no platform API calls, no sleeps, safe to call repeatedly and in dry runs.

stdout_json.name: xpst_backfill
stdout_json.description: Retry failed or incomplete posts from history. `attempted` / `successful` are counts, not a verdict: `batch_status`, `exit_code` and `failed_destinations` report the same aggregate the CLI (`xpst backfill`) exits on, so an all-failed retry is not read as a successful one.

stdout_json.name: xpst_config_show
stdout_json.description: Display current configuration (with sensitive values masked)

stdout_json.name: xpst_auth_status
stdout_json.description: Show live authentication status and the truthful per-platform badge (connected / expiring / needs_reauth / source_only / disabled / unknown). The badge is derived from a live check with its timestamp — a stored credential alone is never reported as connected.

stdout_json.name: xpst_byo_app
stdout_json.description: Bring-your-own developer app setup: report (masked) which platforms have a locally-stored app credential, or store/clear one. A stored app id/secret is what flips a platform into its official OAuth path with NO App Review needed (Meta Standard Access: the owner uses their own app). The secret is stored only in the encrypted local store and is never echoed back — responses carry at most a 4-char id tail. Omit app_id/app_secret for a status read.

stdout_json.name: xpst_bio_get
stdout_json.description: Get the link-in-bio page URL and its current configuration. Returns the public /bio URL, the page handle, and the ordered list of links (enabled social accounts + custom links) exactly as rendered by the dashboard bio page.

stdout_json.name: xpst_capabilities
stdout_json.description: Return the canonical role-aware provider catalog AND the content contract without network calls: per destination, which content types it declares and which it can actually publish (`content`), plus the publishing route each content type takes. Read this before posting so you never attempt a modality a destination cannot publish.

stdout_json.name: xpst_preflight
stdout_json.description: Resolve the per-destination plan BEFORE anything is published: for each destination, whether it will publish (`posted`), is not connected (`skipped_unconnected`, with the connect command), or cannot take this format (`unsupported_format`, with the envelope). Targets an explicit `platforms` list, or `all: true` for every connected account that accepts the format, or the format route ∩ connected accounts. Never uploads and never touches the network

stdout_json.name: xpst_readiness
stdout_json.description: Return local setup readiness and actionable blockers without starting the posting engine

stdout_json.name: xpst_auth_start
stdout_json.description: Return a human-only authentication action plan; never opens a browser or accepts secrets

stdout_json.name: xpst_providers
stdout_json.description: List supported content sources and posting destinations with capabilities

stdout_json.name: xpst_disconnect
stdout_json.description: Disconnect a platform: remove its stored account credentials (tokens, cookies, session files) and set accounts.<platform>.enabled=false. Never touches posted content or local state.

stdout_json.name: xpst_delete
stdout_json.description: Delete a post for REAL on the platform and remove its local record. Calls the platform delete API for every destination the video was posted to and reports each destination's outcome: deleted, soft_hidden (unpublished but recoverable), pending (could not confirm — remove manually via the returned share_url), or unsupported (that platform has no delete path, e.g. Messenger). The response carries platform_deleted per destination plus a boolean aggregate (true only when every destination is gone). Destination platforms (YouTube, X, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, Facebook) all support deletion today. Removing the record also makes the engine treat the video as new again, so treat the call as destructive and confirm with the user first.

stdout_json.name: messenger_send
stdout_json.description: Send a text message to a Messenger recipient (page-scoped PSID) via the Meta Graph API. Requires a configured Messenger Page Access Token (run 'xpst auth messenger'). Returns the message_id.

stdout_json.name: messenger_set_rules
stdout_json.description: Configure the Messenger ManyChat-lite auto-reply rules. Provide a keyword->reply map (the '*' key is the catch-all) and optionally toggle auto_reply. Persists to config.

stdout_json.name: xpst_messenger_check_comments
stdout_json.description: Fetch recent comments on an Instagram or Facebook post and auto-reply per the configured reply_rules (Content360-style comment auto-reply, mirroring `xpst messenger check-comments`). Gated by accounts.messenger.comment_reply_enabled and comment_platforms. Posts public replies on the comment threads when a keyword matches.

stdout_json.name: kb_add
stdout_json.description: Ingest a local file or URL into the knowledge base

stdout_json.name: kb_query
stdout_json.description: Return stored knowledge nuggets whose text matches the query

stdout_json.name: kb_organize
stdout_json.description: Discover areas, tag difficulty, and assign nuggets

stdout_json.name: kb_areas
stdout_json.description: List discovered knowledge areas in course order (beginner -> advanced)

stdout_json.name: xpst_setup_start
stdout_json.description: Start or return the shared resumable setup transaction

stdout_json.name: xpst_setup_status
stdout_json.description: Read the shared setup transaction and pending human actions

stdout_json.name: xpst_setup_resume
stdout_json.description: Resume setup with safe step state or caller-verified readiness

stdout_json.name: xpst_setup_reset
stdout_json.description: Reset the shared setup transaction and its recovery copies

stdout_json.name: xpst_stream
stdout_json.description: Live-stream relay status: every platform's ingest path (api/manual/unsupported), whether a stream key is already stored, and whether xPST holds the credentials to fetch one itself. The same registry and key-presence verdict the CLI serves, so an agent never has to shell out. With `include_live` it also asks Twitch/Kick who is live right now — only for platforms whose credentials exist; the rest come back as `unavailable` with the registration step. Never returns a stream key. Read-only: it stores nothing, posts nothing, spends nothing.

stdout_json.name: xpst_chat
stdout_json.description: Read-only live chat from Twitch, YouTube and Kick as ONE merged timeline. Each message carries `platform`, `author`, `text`, `timestamp`, `message_id` and `channel`, ordered chronologically, so an agent never has to reconcile three feeds. With `read` it opens the platforms for `duration_s` (bounded, default 20s, max 300) and returns what arrived; without it, it reports what COULD be read and what is missing — no network. A platform that cannot be read appears under `unavailable` with a code and the next step, never as an empty list: 'not live', 'no credential' and 'no such channel' are different answers. Never sends, moderates or replies — there is no write path at all.
